title: Port E-001..E-006's acceptance checks (the 14 ledger finish bodies, 6 of them Python, and run_finish_e004_2's look assertions) to Go tests that build and drive the real program over HTTP
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

critique-review missed: M-add-3's prescribed fix (a whole-suite check on `go test -json` events) spoke of 'the set of skipped top-level tests' and never said that a subtest's skip event counts. The built suite() kept only verdicts whose Test name has no '/'. A subtest `t.Skip("CHROME_BIN is not set ...")` under a passing parent, which is the old TestBrowserSkipEndsTheCallingTest shape and E-009 line 2's exact condition, passed TestSuiteInChrome ('277 top-level tests, skipped: []'). It also left TestSuiteWithoutABrowser blind to a skipped acceptance subtest. A check could have been written from this: a corpus row with a skip event on `pkg/TestX/caller` naming CHROME_BIN, which must be refused.

critique missed: The critic's own pattern for M1's assertion-site scan was `\breturn\s+[1-9]\b`. It needs a word boundary after one digit, so `return 124` and `return 10` are not sites. The completeness-by-construction claim that SC-045 deletes the Python on was therefore false for tests/acceptance/run_finish.py L145 (`return 124`, the runner's timeout verdict) and L184 (the run_body call that inherits it). TestPortedAssertionsHaveAGoTest stayed green. A check could have been written from it: a site corpus containing `return 124`, `return (1)`, `return -1` and `else 12`.

critique missed: m2's prescription widened the regex rules but left three spelling holes. (a) The 'acceptance tests neither choose nor start a browser' rule needs a quote right before the flag, so `strings.Fields("--no-first-run --headless=new --remote-debugging-port=0")` and `fmt.Sprintf("%s --user-data-dir=%s about:blank", ...)` pass. (b) The DevTools-driver rule matches only os./syscall. readers, so `(&exec.Cmd{}).Environ()` passes. The critique had already named CC-001 variants as the failure class, yet O-021 was marked 'closed as a class'. A check could have been written from it: fire rows for those three spellings in internal/fitnessrules/testdata/rule_spellings.json.

critique missed: m2's by-construction backstop (`go list -deps -test ./tests/acceptance/... ./internal/testutil/...`) was prescribed without build tags. tests/acceptance/breaks (sc042breaks) and tests/acceptance/suite (sc042suite) appear in `go list` only with -tags. A tagged acceptance file that imports a product package in a spelling the regexes pin quiet passes both guards, while the fitness because-texts say such holes are 'caught by construction'. A check could have been written from it: run `go list` once more with -tags "sc042breaks sc042suite" and apply the same allow-list.

critique-review missed: Running the inner `go test -count=1 -json ./...` inside the sc042suite-tagged package inherits the caller's GOFLAGS unchanged. A GOFLAGS carrying -tags=sc042suite makes the suite re-run itself recursively, and -tags=sc042breaks adds the seven-build breaks test. The design already strips -tags in the sibling breaks test (baseGoFlags, breaks_test.go:161-172), but nothing said the new whole-suite check needs the same. A check could have been written from it: a test that sets GOFLAGS=-tags=sc042suite and expects the inner run not to start the suite again.

critique missed: The design's component list had no page-reader library, although every one of the six Python bodies carries its own prelude of page readers (Count, Vote, Dislikes, Say, Part, Visible, Shown, Own, Depth, Mine). The builder added program/reader.go, html.go and expect.go. That left a second forgiving HTML parser (program/html.go beside internal/testutil/e002row's Node/Dom) that the design never planned for. The critique had flagged the six bodies as unread (M2) but did not ask what shared helpers they would need.

still unknown: Do E-009 lines 4 and 5 pass against the committed acceptance packages? Those finish bodies (exit-at-start program, GOFLAGS overlay breaks, held 127.0.0.1:8080, dead proxies, link-none, repo left clean) are planted only at epic finish. The slice's own TestStartIgnoresTheDefaultPortAndProxies, TestStartLeavesNothingInTheRepository and the breaks test mimic them, but nobody ran the planted bodies themselves.

still unknown: Does anything under `go test ./...` read the .py files or tests/acceptance/__pycache__? Validation proved the editions of the in-tree Python by its own script. The design says the table never needs the deleted files, and only SC-045 deleting them and running the suite will show it.

still unknown: Which architecture block owns tests/acceptance/** (including suite/testdata and ported/testdata)? AA-043 was rejected, so the packages have no owner in the record. A person has to decide whether any block owns them.

went wrong: Both repro rounds failed at launch with WinError 206 (command line too long) and produced no findings. Repro passed with 'nothing checkable', so that stage contributed nothing.

went wrong: The stages before the build could not enumerate the assertions. The survey recorded approximate counts ('16/14/15/19/10/23') and the title's '14 bodies' was really 16 (10 Go, 6 Python). The design said the six Python bodies were unread, and the critique had no ledger access. M1 and M2 were both majors, and the independent list only appeared as the builder's first step.

went wrong: Four holes in prescribed fixes reached the build and were found only by code review #1: the single-digit `return` regex, the top-level-only skip events, `go list` without -tags, and rules 3/4 that missed three spellings. The skip-events hole sent the slice back to build 3. The spelling-class closure (O-021) leaked again as IN-m2, which was waived to SC-047.

went wrong: Three of the six waived or deferred code-review findings (IN-m3, IN-m4, m5) have no reproduction, so nothing in the engine will turn them into work unless a run fails. Until then the fitness because-texts keep claiming 'caught by construction' for build-tagged files, and the new one-command suite has never been run twice in a row.

went wrong: No person triaged anything: all 11 critique, 4 critique-review and 6 code-review #2 findings were disposed by a model ('counted as untriaged'). Code-review #1 never opened 15 of 49 changed files whole (the ten E-001/E-002 ports, E-005, E-006 x2, one snapshot), and the engine had to send it back to 18 unseen hunks.
went wrong: The design retier raised the risk to high but nobody resized the slice. A medium slice produced 67 file-changes across two builds, 3 builds and 3 reviews.
